basis: Developmental disability, congenital heart defects and generalized hypertrichosis define syndrome; scoliosis occurs in 3/10 patients; ocular abnormalities below 30%.
Syndrome defined by progressive dilated cardiomyopathy and childhood sensorineural hearing loss, both present in 80-99%.
Disordered trimethylamine metabolism; urinary, sweat and breath excretion causes odor without intrinsic renal, skin or pulmonary damage.
Benign neoplasm arising predominantly in salivary glands; uncommon respiratory tract sites do not characterize most patients.
Concept describes a vascular response to isoproterenol; no definition or evidence establishes additional organ disease.
Thiamine transport/metabolism disorder causing basal ganglia injury and encephalopathy; dysphagia and ophthalmoplegia reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Melanoma arising within the cornea; no common additional organ involvement specified.
Inflammation confined to the reproductive endocervix; an infectious or autoimmune cause is not specified.
Squamous intraepithelial neoplasia involving the cornea.
Localized inherited skin blistering with nail dystrophy or loss; systemic damage of severe generalized forms does not apply.
Defined by tremor/movement disorder and duodenal ulceration; nystagmus accompanies the neurologic syndrome without established intrinsic eye damage.
Autoimmune neuromuscular-junction disease; ocular and bulbar weakness are neurologic. Myositis is a separate overlap disorder; respiratory failure occurs in 5-29%.
Multiple tumors arising from spinal meninges.
Central dopaminergic dysfunction causes rigidity, altered consciousness and dysautonomia; acidosis is acute systemic stress; rhabdomyolysis and kidney injury occur in 5-29%.
Intellectual disability and obesity define syndrome; sensorineural hearing loss occurs in 4/7. Eyelid dysmorphism lacks demonstrated functional impairment; macroorchidism is reproductive.
Radial/vertebral and ear defects define syndrome; cardiac defects 80-99%, renal malformations 30-79%; oral clefts and cognitive impairment omitted by cap; eye/lung defects 5-29%.
Deficiency of a plasma factor responsible for clot retraction indicates a haemostatic disorder; no additional organ involvement established.
Extraskeletal sarcoma originates in mediastinal soft tissue; no origin in bone, locomotor connective tissue, lung or another axis organ is specified.
Bilateral congenital absence of thigh and lower leg with retained feet is a structural limb and skeletal malformation.
Immunodeficiency and learning/motor impairment define syndrome; recurrent respiratory infections are secondary diseases; pulmonary fibrosis occurs in 5-29%.
Umbrella for rhabditid nematode infections; affected organs vary across subtypes, without a shared organ site established for most patients.
Cutaneous mucinosis with diagnostic monoclonal gammopathy; myopathy and esophageal dysfunction with dysphagia occur in 30-79%; renal, cardiac, pulmonary and CNS findings are below 30%.
Disorder directly affecting peripheral nerve axons; no additional organ damage shared across this umbrella.
Benign diffuse proliferation of blood vessels; infectious mechanisms apply to particular subtypes rather than the entire umbrella.
MVK-related autoinflammation; oral ulcers 60%, GI hemorrhage 80-99%, arthritis 67%; vasculitis 30-79% omitted by cap; transient rash and organomegaly do not establish lasting damage.
